tasks.short: Advise management on equal opportunity, harassment and discrimination, especially where pay and benefits are involved.

steps.what: Clarify the management question, affected people and immediate concerns.
Retrieve relevant policies, agreements and authorised employee records.
Assess the facts and prepare advice, consulting legal counsel when needed.

loop.input: Case scope and authorised case references, with source identifiers and effective dates.
loop.output: Advice brief separating established facts, missing facts, policy references and questions for legal counsel.
loop.check: Check source identifiers and quotations automatically. The manager checks applicability, omissions and conclusions before sharing.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per brief. Missing or conflicting sources return to manual assessment.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the brief, but varied allegations and policy wording require free-text reading.

steps.what: Explain options, challenge assumptions and agree next steps with management.
Record advice, action owners and follow-up dates in the restricted case file.

tasks.design: A restricted workspace in the {WORKFLOW} retrieves approved references from the {DOCS} and authorised records from the {HCM}; selected files support a pilot without connectors. A bounded model drafts a cited advice brief for manager approval before sharing. Confirmed actions populate the case record and follow-up tasks in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sensitive records were scattered, policy versions were difficult to track, and bespoke advice resisted simple templates.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing permissions, search and task configuration cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and templates; bounded drafting helps with varied text.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting accounts, legal interpretation and management resistance remain human work. GDPR applies to sensitive records, and significant staff decisions require safeguards under Article 22 [S10]. National rules govern consultation and employment procedures; the EU AI Act assessment depends on the intended use.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise power imbalances, challenge discriminatory reasoning and deliver difficult advice with trust and discretion.

ambition.what: An early discrimination check for proposed pay and benefits policy changes.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less reference gathering and record entry, with more time for early policy advice. Decision rights do not change automatically; management and legal counsel retain their existing authority.

reach.task: Review whether a proposed benefits rule disadvantages a protected group.
reach.learn: Indirect discrimination, appropriate comparison groups and safe handling of sensitive evidence.

reach.task: Prepare consultation on a proposed reward policy change.
reach.learn: Collective agreement interpretation and national consultation requirements.

evidence.claim: Permission-controlled reference retrieval and structured follow-up can use existing configuration; bespoke drafting needs a bounded loop.
Article 22 is relevant when automation alone produces legally or similarly significant decisions about staff.
The Danish study reported 2.8% hours saved across its sample; it does not validate these task estimates.

assumptions: The manager advises on reward implications; harassment investigations may belong to another HR role.
Today’s time shares are estimates, informed by the priors and the substantial advisory conversation.
remaining_pct values are design estimates, not measured savings.
The pilot uses approved documents and excludes automatic decisions about individual employees.
Build ranges cover one language and one policy set, with existing identity and access controls.
The consent and access range includes employee or works-council consultation where national rules require it; elapsed waiting may be longer.
unknowns: Which countries, collective agreements and consultation arrangements apply?
Who owns investigations, legal advice and decisions about individual staff?
Are policy documents versioned and employee records accessible through approved interfaces?
What retention periods and access restrictions apply to case records?
How much time is currently spent preparing advice rather than discussing it?
research_questions: Which common questions can be answered through approved policy links without model drafting?
Does a source-linked brief reduce preparation time without increasing unsupported conclusions?
Which intended uses would trigger EU AI Act requirements or additional national consultation?
new_work: Review draft briefs for missing facts, inappropriate conclusions and outdated sources.
Maintain approved policy versions and access permissions.
Handle failed retrievals and conflicting references.
Check that follow-up tasks contain only necessary case information.

tasks.short: Represent the employer in personnel hearings and investigations, especially disputes involving pay and benefits.

steps.what: Gather authorised employee records, correspondence and reward calculations relevant to the case.
Agree the representation mandate, disputed issues and preparation needs with legal counsel.
Prepare a chronology, evidence index and hearing brief from the case documents.

loop.input: Authorised case documents and representation mandate, with stable document identifiers.
loop.output: Source-linked events, evidence index and a templated hearing brief with disputed statements clearly attributed.
loop.check: Validate document identifiers and dates. The manager checks completeness, attribution and disputed events against originals.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document. Unreadable or contradictory material goes to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Indexing and layout are deterministic, but events and assertions occur in varied correspondence and narrative documents.

steps.what: Review the brief and decide what evidence may be disclosed.
Send the approved evidence bundle to the designated hearing or investigation recipient.
Attend the hearing or investigation, explain evidence and respond within the agreed mandate.
Record the outcome, assign follow-up actions and update the restricted case file.

loop.input: Manager-authored hearing notes and the recorded hearing outcome.
loop.output: Draft case update and proposed follow-up tasks, with references to the notes.
loop.check: The manager verifies commitments, owners and dates. No deadline or admission may be inferred.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass. Ambiguous commitments remain unassigned for manual clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative hearing notes need interpretation before they become structured actions.

tasks.design: A restricted case workspace joins authorised records from the {HCM}, {PAYROLL}, {DOCS} and {EMAIL}, or accepts selected exports. Deterministic indexing and a bounded extraction loop prepare source-linked hearing materials; legal counsel decides disclosure scope and approves the recipient and exact bundle before the {WORKFLOW} sends it through the {EMAIL}. Reviewed hearing notes create the case update and follow-up tasks in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence crossed several systems, documents used inconsistent formats, and disclosure required legal judgement. Low case volume often made a dedicated integration difficult to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable connectors, document indexing and templates cover the mechanical work. AI-assisted coding makes a small shared case workspace cheaper to build, while bounded extraction helps assemble narrative evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, contested facts, privilege and live questioning remain difficult. GDPR governs personal and special-category data; national rules govern hearings, representation and disclosure. Assess EU AI Act obligations for the actual use, particularly if the tool expands into employee evaluation.
tasks.human_edge: Give credible evidence, recognise when a question exceeds the mandate and respond calmly under challenge.
tasks.altitude: Preparation becomes shorter and more traceable, but hearings and legal review still dominate the work. Representation, settlement and disclosure rights remain within the existing mandate.

reach.task: Prepare a hearing chronology and identify unresolved procedural questions.
reach.learn: National hearing procedures, collective agreements and limits on the representation mandate.

reach.task: Reconstruct disputed pay amounts from historical payroll records.
reach.learn: Historical pay rules, correction records and evidence traceability.

evidence.claim: Evidence retrieval, indexing and submission routing can be deterministic; narrative chronology preparation needs reviewed extraction.
Representation at a contested hearing requires human judgement and communication; the digest provides no case validating its automation.
The Danish study found modest aggregate hours saved and unchanged earnings and hours; hearing-specific gains were not established.

assumptions: The manager participates mainly in cases involving reward expertise; legal counsel or labor relations leads legal procedure.
Time shares describe the whole task across participants, including counsel's review.
The priors support retaining representation; the decomposition exposes smaller preparation gains.
remaining_pct values are estimates to test, not documented outcomes.
The pilot covers one hearing procedure and existing document formats.
Build ranges are standalone estimates; sharing the first task's workspace may reduce effort.
Consent and access work includes consultation where national rules require it; formal waiting periods may exceed the range.
Hearings may also occur by call; no recording or transcription is assumed.
unknowns: How often does this manager represent the employer, and in which forums?
Who approves disclosure and who holds settlement authority?
Can historical records and correspondence be retrieved with reliable identifiers?
Which evidence formats, submission channels and deadlines apply?
What privilege, retention and consultation arrangements apply?
Does case volume justify connectors rather than selected exports?
research_questions: Can an export-based pilot deliver enough preparation value before building integrations?
How often does chronology extraction omit evidence or confuse allegations with established facts?
Which submission routes support exact bundle approval and a reliable receipt?
new_work: Check extracted events against original evidence and resolve contradictions.
Review disclosure bundles, recipients and redactions before release.
Maintain source links, access permissions and retention rules.
Handle unavailable records and failed submissions.
Verify proposed follow-up actions against actual hearing commitments.

role.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting references and assembling case materials, while retaining sensitive advice and representation. The change itself grants no new legal or employment decision rights.
reach: Work with equal opportunity representatives on early discrimination checks for reward changes.
Support labor relations specialists with traceable hearing preparation.
Work with payroll and timekeeping clerks to reconstruct disputed pay.
skills_to_grow: Discrimination analysis in pay and benefits
role.ambitious_version: Offer an early discrimination check during reward policy design, so management can address concerns before proposals reach consultation or become disputes.
